environments.description:
Deployment targets, by name. Optional: a project that only ever passes
`--db` explicitly needs none.

dev.description:
The optional dev database (SPEC §9.3). Absent means previews stay
offline, which is the default and a supported way to work.

max_data_rows.description:
How many rows a `data:` block may declare before `validate` says this
does not look like reference data (ADR-0004).

A knob rather than a constant because the line between a lookup table
and somebody's business table is a judgement about *this* project — but
it is a warning either way, never a refusal: pbps does not get to decide
that a 1,200-row currency table is illegitimate.

policies.description:
The organization's own rules and their suppressions (ADR-0008). Absent
means every built-in rule at its default severity.

DialectName.description:
The target database dialect.

A project is bound to exactly one dialect. "Supports multiple databases" means
the tool can drive different databases, not that one set of declarations
deploys to both (SPEC §1.3).

Environment.description:
One deployment target.

# Why there is no `url:` field

A connection string carries a password, and `pbps.yml` is committed to git.
The config therefore names the **environment variable** that holds the
string, never the string. This is not an inconvenience to be worked around
with a second, undocumented field: an inline `url:` would be a credential in
version control, and the one thing worse than not having the feature is
having it and being surprised by it.

url_env.description:
The name of the environment variable holding the ADO.NET connection
string, e.g. `PROD_CONN`.

description.description: Shown by `pbps status`, for humans reading a list of environments.

Hooks.description:
Exec points (SPEC §9.4): pbps runs a command, and the command does the
talking.

There are no Slack or Teams integrations here on purpose. An exec hook
outlives any chat API, holds no credentials of its own, and lets a team
deliver drift alerts through whatever they already run.

on_apply.description:
Run after a successful `apply`, with the unchanged plan JSON on stdin.

This is the original hook contract. Use `on_apply_attempt` for a
versioned event that also reports failed attempts.

on_apply_attempt.description:
Run after either outcome of an `apply`, with a versioned event JSON on
stdin containing the plan path, checksum, outcome and ledger entry or
error.

on_drift.description: Run when `verify` finds drift, with the drift report JSON on stdin.

Unmanaged.description:
How to treat objects in the database that the declarations do not mention
(SPEC §8.2).

`Ignore` is the default because it is the precondition for gradual adoption:
pbps has to be able to share a database with tooling that was there first.

Dev.description:
The optional throwaway engine of SPEC §9.3.

# Why it is always optional

The air-gap promise stands: with no dev database the preview degrades to
lightweight normalization and says so. This differs from Atlas, where a dev
database is required for many operations — and the difference is deliberate,
because a tool that cannot answer without Docker cannot be used where this
one has to be.

A dev-verified plan is still a **preview**. Applyable plans come only from
`plan --db` against the target, and this does not move that line.

url_env.description:
The name of an environment variable holding a connection string to a
throwaway server — never the string itself, for the reason
[`Environment`] gives.

docker.description:
A container image to start and throw away, e.g.
`mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest`.

Policies.description:
The whole block. Absent means every rule at its default and nothing
suppressed.

rules.description:
Rule id to its setting.

A map in Rust, a closed list of keys in the editor schema: see
[`rules_schema`]. `BTreeMap<String, _>` derives to "any key", which
blessed `naming.tabel` in the editor and left the typo to be found by
`pbps validate` — the opposite of what a generated schema is for
(DECISIONS 172).

naming.table.description: Checks a table's name (without its schema) matches `pattern`. Takes pattern.

pattern.description: A regular expression the name must match in full.

naming.column.description: Checks a column's name matches `pattern`. Takes pattern.

pattern.description: A regular expression the name must match in full.

naming.index.description: Checks an index's name matches `pattern`. Takes pattern.

pattern.description: A regular expression the name must match in full.

naming.constraint.description: Checks a named constraint (primary key, unique, foreign key, check) matches `pattern`. Takes pattern.

pattern.description: A regular expression the name must match in full.

data.max-rows.description: Checks a `data:` block declares at most `rows` rows — past that it stops looking like reference data (ADR-0004). Takes rows.

rows.description: The row count above which a block is reported.

column.no-deprecated-type.description: Checks a column does not use a type the engine has deprecated (text, ntext, image).

change.expand-contract.description: Checks one revision does not both add and drop or narrow in the same table, which usually wants expand/contract staging (SPEC §13.3).

change.narrowing-on-data.description: Checks a type narrowing depends on the data already stored; the pre-flight probe measures it at apply time.

grant.widen.description: Checks a grant widens what a role can do (ADR-0005), for a project that wants the label at a severity of its own.

change.window.description: Checks a connected plan is computed inside an allowed change window: `offset` (`+08:00`) and `allow` (`mon-fri 09:00-17:00`, ...). Takes offset, allow.

offset.description: The UTC offset the windows are written in (`+08:00`).

Suppression.description: One suppression: a rule that does not fire, where, why, and until when.

on.description:
The object it applies to (`dbo.customer`, `role app_reader`). Absent
means the whole project.

reason.description: Why. The field an audit reads; blank is refused.

until.description:
`YYYY-MM-DD`. From that day on the suppression stops applying and the
finding comes back at its configured severity (ADR-0008 decision 4).
